subject.title: Reject unsupported diagnostics OTel grpc config

question: Should this PR land the narrow `http/protobuf`-only config contract with doctor migration, or should OpenClaw keep `grpc` as a config value until real gRPC exporter support exists?
rationale: The code repair is coherent, but removing a shipped config enum value and deciding whether doctor should disable enabled telemetry is a maintainer-owned compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Land narrow rejection with doctor repair
options.body: Accept the compatibility tradeoff because current runtime never exported `grpc`, and doctor preserves the no-export outcome for active OTLP signals.

options.title: Pause for real gRPC support
options.body: Keep `grpc` in the config contract only if maintainers want to implement and test real gRPC exporters instead of rejecting the value.

options.title: Change migration semantics first
options.body: If disabling enabled configs is not acceptable, revise the doctor migration to a different explicit maintainer-approved upgrade behavior before merge.

recommendation.title: Land narrow rejection with doctor repair
recommendation.body: Accept the compatibility tradeoff because current runtime never exported `grpc`, and doctor preserves the no-export outcome for active OTLP signals.

likelyOwner.reason: The original diagnostics exporter/config surface traces to steipete, making them the best available owner for the compatibility direction if maintainer intent is needed.
